question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
{sec}^{2}⁡x-1={tan}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity

$$
1-{sech}^{2}⁡x={tanh}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{sech}^{2}⁡x}{1-{sech}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{sech}^{2}⁡x}{{tanh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{csch}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{coth}⁡x\,{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =-\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)+\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-1}+\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-1} \\  & =-\frac{{3}^{2}+1}{{3}^{2}-1}+\frac{{2}^{2}+1}{{2}^{2}-1} \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}+\frac{5}{3} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
